observations: Photo 0 shows a used metal automatic transmission/gearbox assembly removed from a vehicle, sitting on a concrete floor.
Another engine component (partial, with a pulley and timing cover) is visible in the background, not clearly part of this listing.
Visible surface rust/oxidation on parts of the transmission case and exposed sensor wiring with a connector (electrical plug) dangling from the unit.
No part number, VIN tag, casting number, or brand marking is legible anywhere on the metal housing in this photo.
A watermark reading 'LOTCHDAVID INVESTMENT LTD' is overlaid on the image; this is a seller/shop stamp, not proof of the part's identity or condition.
No fluid, no torque converter visible attached, no photo of the full unit from other angles, no test or installation shown.

claims.claim: Fits Toyota Highlander and Sienna, 2017 and above
claims.evidence: No part number, casting mark, or vehicle tag is visible in photo 0 to confirm make/model/year fitment.
The wiring connector is partially visible in photo 0 but pin count cannot be counted or confirmed from this image.
No output shaft configuration or drive-type marking is visible or countable in photo 0.

risks.risk: Fitment to the claimed vehicle/year (Highlander/Sienna 2017+) may be wrong, which would make the part unusable to the buyer.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the manufacturer's part/ID tag or casting number stamped on the transmission case.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unconfirmed fitment / generic used unit, not as a guaranteed exact-fit part

risks.risk: Internal working condition (shifting, gear wear, torque converter condition, fluid contamination) cannot be judged from an external photo.
risks.proof: Video of the unit being bench-tested or running in a vehicle, plus a photo/video of the drained fluid.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / condition unknown

risks.risk: Visible rust suggests possible water exposure or long outdoor storage, which can mean internal corrosion or seal damage not visible from outside.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all mounting faces, seals, and the fluid pan/drain plug area.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having probable internal corrosion risk

risks.risk: Connector/pin count (claimed 30-pin) cannot be verified, and a wrong pin count would mean it is electrically incompatible with the buyer's vehicle harness.
risks.proof: Close, well-lit photo of the connector face showing countable pins, ideally next to a ruler or coin for scale.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unconfirmed pin-count / possible incompatibility

risks.risk: Completeness is unknown — torque converter, mounts, sensors, or bell housing bolts could be missing, which affects installable value.
risks.proof: Photos from at least three more angles (front bell housing, rear output, underside) showing all ports and components present.
risks.if_unproven: priced as incomplete unit unless all components are shown

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the OEM part/ID tag or casting number on the transmission case.
Clear photo of the electrical connector showing a countable number of pins.
Video of the unit being tested (bench spin test or installed and shifting).
Photos from additional angles: bell housing face, output shaft/flange, underside/pan, and fluid level/color.
Any paperwork or vehicle the part was pulled from (e.g., a photo of the donor vehicle's VIN plate).
response.reason: The photo shows a genuine used automotive transmission/gearbox, so it can be identified and priced by type at worst case (unconfirmed fitment, condition untested, completeness unverified) even though the seller's specific vehicle, pin-count, and drive-type claims are unverifiable from the image.
